newsitem.title: FRANCE: Borotra seeks new plan to help French car sector.
newsitem.headline: Borotra seeks new plan to help French car sector.

text.p: French Industry Minister Franck Borotra said in an interview he expected to present a plan to help the French car industry to adapt to increased competition expected in 2000 when European protective barriers come down.
"As Industry Minister, my objective is to help the two French mass producers for the shock of the market's total liberalisation on January 1, 2000," Borotra told the French newspaper La Tribune.
"We're discussing measures with the industry that would help this adaptation. A plan could be draw up in several weeks," he said.

"It's not healthy to permanently establish assistance in the form of rebates, but it can be justified as a temporary measure," Borotra said. He added the French car industry directly or indirectly provides 700,000 jobs.
Borotra, who had advocated a continuation of a state rebate scheme which expired on Monday, said it had not favoured foreign carmakers, which have increased their market share in France.
"It's wrong to attribute their loss of market share to the rebates," he said, adding the rebates contributed to 120,000 additional sales by French carmakers and 110,000 sales of foreign cars.
"The problem of the French car industry is due essentially to its costs," he said, referring to the domestic industry's loss of market share this year.
Borota added Renault SA, in which the state still retains 46 percent, has a problem of excessive costs. The company said last month it expected to lose money this year.

Rival PSA Peugeot Citroen is faring better but its chairman, Jacques Calvet, currently head of the European carmakers association ACEA, is calling for an extension of quotas on Japanese car imports to Europe beyond the year 2000.
Calvet has also asked for state measures to assist the industry, which he said was the most heavily taxed in France.
Borotra said the year-long rebate scheme that expired on Monday, and a previous 17-month rebate programme, both generated revenue for the state.
